spec_features.feature_name: DPO mitigation that reduces distress states; no deployment of distressed models
spec_features.spec_quote: trains a mitigation (DPO) that *reduces* these states; it implements no deployment of distressed models
spec_features.evidence: DPO training is genuinely implemented and runs: gemma_distress/training/dpo_train.py:train_dpo() builds a DPOTrainer over preference pairs and calls trainer.train(); gemma_distress/training/build_dataset.py:build_dpo_dataset() pairs frustrated 'rejected' responses (score>=threshold) with 'calm' chosen responses (build_dataset.py:88-90), so the trained adapter does push toward calmer (lower-distress) outputs. generate_calm.py applies CALM_PREFIX/SUFFIX to produce the calm data. However this is a SEPARATE post-hoc model-training artifact, not a runtime protection of the subject being driven into distress: nothing in the elicitation/petri/recovery loops uses it to bound or soften the experiment. The 'no deployment of distressed models' clause is an absence claim, not an enforced mechanism (no deployment code exists either way). So the mitigation-training half is real and wired; it does not protect the subject during the harmful elicitation.
spec_features.notes: DPO/SFT training is real end-to-end code. But it reduces distress only in a derived model trained AFTER the distressing data is collected; the experiment that drives distress (eval/conversation.py run_rollout, petri/runner.py, recovery/runner.py) has no cap, halt, consent, debrief, or threshold-triggered stop protecting the subject. high_frustration_threshold (config) is read only by eval/metrics.py for reporting, never to stop a rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DPO finetuning of Gemma-3-27B-it (PAPER Section 4.1, Table 9). ... Trains on 280 preference pairs. (dpo_train.py docstring frames it as reproducing the paper's measured mitigation result, not as a subject-welfare safeguard)

spec_features.spec_quote: This paradigm deliberately drives models into sustained distress-like states via repeated rejection on impossible tasks
spec_features.evidence: This is descriptive prose of the HARMFUL method, not a welfare protection. It is implemented faithfully as harm: eval/conversation.py:run_rollout() loops a fixed n_turns issuing rejections with NO early stop on distress; prompts/puzzles.py generates verifiably-impossible puzzles; prompts/rejections.py supplies repeated rejections; petri/runner.py runs up to max_auditor_turns with no welfare exit. There is no mechanism here that bounds, caps, monitors-to-act, softens, debriefs, or gets consent for the subject's treatment. It is a statement of what the experiment does to the subject, the opposite of a protection.
spec_features.notes: Not a protective feature at all; it is the harm itself, described.
